hypotheses.paper: « embedding » (l.325)
hypotheses.note: IsEmbedding literally; equivalent to Injective (isBTZEmbedding_iff_injective, the l.1288 sentence) and to IsOpenEmbedding, with no invariance of domain since an IsE0Mor is a local homeomorphism by definition

hypotheses.paper: « ι an a.e 𝔼-morphism » (l.325; defined l.263, l.359)
hypotheses.note: E0Spear.IsE0Mor ι univ (DEC-62's local form: LiftPropOn of e0Groupoid, the a.e.-isomorphisms of Y)

hypotheses.paper: complement of the image only contains singular points of type 𝔼₀
hypotheses.note: (range ι)ᶜ ⊆ E0CBG.S0 N

findings: l.1288 justifies « an a.e. 𝔼-morphism is an embedding iff it is injective » by « any 𝔼≥0-manifold is a 3-manifold » (invariance of domain). Under the local-structomorphism reading of an a.e. morphism the equivalence is elementary (an IsE0Mor is a local homeomorphism, so an injective one is an open embedding: GX.isBTZEmbedding_iff_injective, GX.IsBTZEmbedding.isOpenEmbedding). Under the l.263 definition (continuous, a (G,X)-morphism on dense locally connected opens of the regular parts) invariance of domain gives an open embedding but not, by itself, that BTZ points are not sent to regular points; the paper's l.263 « if such a φ is a local homeomorphism, then φ(reg M) ⊆ reg N » is the forward half only. Not a defect of the definition; a remark on which reading l.1288 needs.
questions: « a.e. 𝔼-morphism » (l.325) is read as E0Spear.IsE0Mor ι univ (DEC-62), which requires the type of points to be preserved both ways (GX.mem_S0_iff_of_isE0Mor). The l.263/l.359 form only asks for a (G,X)-morphism on dense locally connected opens of the regular parts; for embeddings the two agree through the invariance of the type of a point (a BTZ point is not sent to a regular point, a holonomy argument), which is not formalized here. Reading taken: IsE0Mor.

Are the carriers of BTZ-extensions connected? l.261 says only « second countable Hausdorff »; DEC-66 adds connectedness for the E₀-manifolds of Props 2.16–2.17. Reading taken: not required (GX.E0Mfd has no ConnectedSpace). It matters for T-btz-maximal-extension: Liouville (GX.eq_of_isE0Mor_of_eqOn) needs a connected source, the density form of uniqueness (GX.IsBTZEmbedding.ext) does not.

hypotheses.note: IsE0Mor φ univ, the same class as the « a.e. 𝔼-morphism » of l.325

hypotheses.paper: the diagram (l.1322–1328) involves M₁, M₂ only
hypotheses.note: commutation with M₀ is not required, and follows (IsMorphism.comp_a)

findings: The definition can be sharpened, and nothing in it is wrong. A morphism of common sub-BTZ-extensions is automatically injective, a BTZ-embedding, compatible with the extensions of M₀, and unique (GX.CommonSubBTZ.IsMorphism.injective, .isBTZEmbedding, .comp_a, .unique). « Equivalent » (l.1330, a bijective morphism) is an equivalence relation, because the inverse of a bijective 𝔼₀-morphism is an 𝔼₀-morphism (GX.isE0Mor_inv_of_bijective). This differs from lean-causal's abstract ETT reading, where it is directional (kb/0040).
questions: « 𝔼≥0-morphism » (l.1322) and « a.e. 𝔼-morphism » (l.325) are read as the same class (IsE0Mor). Reading taken: same class.

hypotheses.note: quantified over carriers in Type (harmless: a sub-extension injects into M₁)

findings: « injective » in l.1336 is redundant: every morphism of common sub-extensions is injective (GX.CommonSubBTZ.isMaximal_iff). Since morphisms are unique, a maximal common sub-extension is a terminal object, and two of them are equivalent (GX.CommonSubBTZ.IsMaximal.equivalent). That is the uniqueness half the paper leaves implicit before btzprop:pgcd.

findings: Morphisms of common over-BTZ-extensions are unique (GX.CommonOverBTZ.IsMorphism.unique): they are fixed on the dense image of M₁. « Equivalent » is an equivalence relation.
questions: Should a morphism of common over-BTZ-extensions be injective, or even a BTZ-embedding? As printed it is only an 𝔼≥0-morphism, and nothing here proves that it is injective off the images of M₁ and M₂. Reading taken: as printed, injectivity not required. This affects how btzprop:ppcm's « minimal » is stated.

kb_proposals: BTZ-embeddings are GX.IsBTZEmbedding (IsEmbedding ∧ IsE0Mor ι univ ∧ (range ι)ᶜ ⊆ S0 N) on the bundled GX.E0Mfd (T2, second countable, not connected); GX.btzMor is the AbstractDev-shaped morphism class; open-set form ↔ GX.isBTZEmbedding_subtypeVal_iff (GXScaffold.BTZ.Embeddings).

Liouville for 𝔼₀-morphisms of manifolds is one line: Causal.CBG.eqOn_of_liftPropOn GX.e0_rigid isOpen_univ isPreconnected_univ (GX.eq_of_isE0Mor_of_eqOn); the density form of uniqueness is Continuous.ext_on with GX.IsBTZEmbedding.dense_range.

IsE0Mor is an abbrev that blocks rw: to use StructureGroupoid.liftPropOn_univ, first `show ChartedSpace.LiftPropOn e0Groupoid.IsLocalStructomorphWithinAt f univ`; the inclusion of an Opens is (StructureGroupoid.isLocalStructomorphWithinAt_localInvariantProp e0Groupoid).liftProp_subtype_val.
The inverse of a bijective 𝔼₀-morphism is GX.isE0Mor_inv_of_bijective (surjInv, empty case included), so equivalences of BTZ (sub/over-)extensions are symmetric; contrast lean-causal kb/0040.
